engine_step_at_issue: The 'older child' step: the engine treated MAGI of 2.13× FPL as within NC's 211% limit for ages 6–18 (plus the 5-point disregard) without checking that the 133–211% band is the CHIP-funded optional targeted low-income child group (42 CFR 435.229), which excludes children covered under a group health plan. Child 1 has employer-sponsored insurance.
summary: Child 1 is 11 and has employer-sponsored insurance all year. Federally, NC can cover children aged 6–18 only up to 133% FPL in the mandatory group under 42 CFR 435.118 (138% with the 5-point disregard), because its historical Medicaid level for that age group was no higher. The 133–211% band, the former NC Health Choice population, came into Medicaid in 2023 as Medicaid-expansion CHIP under the optional targeted low-income child group (42 CFR 435.229), and that group's definition in 42 CFR 435.4 excludes any child covered under a group health plan. The engine took MAGI of 2.13× FPL and tested it against the 211% older-child limit plus the disregard without looking at the child's coverage. With ESI, the 133% group is the only one that applies, and 213% FPL is above it, so Child 1 is not eligible (0), which matches stage 1 and the consensus.
